subject: Recap + benchmark links from today's model-fit call
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Park <lisa@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + benchmark links from today's model-fit call

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for taking the time to chat this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side based on what you shared:

Summary of requirements
- Primary workload: customer support triage + short-form summarization (~50-200 tokens)
- Peak concurrency: ~200 concurrent requests, typical seq len ~128, occasional 512 tokens for long context
- SLOs: P95 latency <150ms, stable throughput during peak windows
- Data concerns: no PII in training, logs must be auditable (retention 90 days)

Initial model recommendations
- redwood/trimmed-instruct-7B (quantized): best cost/latency balance for high throughput
- redwood/llama-13b-opt (float16): higher quality for summarization, good for canary runs

What we shared today
- Prompt set for your evals: acme_eval_prompt_set_v1.csv (attached)
- Redwood-verified performance profile: redwood_benchmarks_acme_20260630.pdf (attached) and live dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-20260630
  - Example perf highlights from our runs (seq len 128):
    • trimmed-instruct-7B (quantized) — sustained throughput 120 TPS (batch_size=8), p50 28ms, p95 95ms, p99 180ms
    • llama-13b-opt (fp16) — sustained throughput 35 TPS, p50 70ms, p95 160ms, p99 320ms

Quality & regression notes
- We ran the prompt set you provided across the two recommended variants and include per-prompt quality deltas in the PDF.
- Redwood Console will alert on quality regressions tied to a prompt set you select; we can wire your baseline prompts to the "Acme - baseline" eval to trigger alerts if accuracy drops >2% on key metrics.

Next steps (proposed)
1) You run the attached prompt set on your side or we can run it for you (we have a sandbox account).
2) We provision a short trial (14 days) on Hosted with dedicated throughput to match your concurrency for a smoke test.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow up next week to review results + discuss procurement/SLA.

Attachments:
- acme_eval_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompt set & labels)
- redwood_benchmarks_acme_20260630.pdf (verified perf + per-prompt quality)

If that plan looks good I can schedule the follow-up and get the trial spun up.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--

Thanks Alex — this is really helpful. A couple clarifying questions before we run the prompt set: 

1) For trimmed-instruct-7B (quantized) — can you share the latency percentiles at seq length 512 (p50/p95/p99) and what batching/concurrency settings were used to collect the 120 TPS number?
2) For the higher-quality variant (llama-13b-opt) — any suggestions on batching and token budget to keep p95 <200ms?
3) On quality monitoring: will we get access to raw request/response logs for deeper analysis, or are the drift/quality alerts aggregated metrics only? We have internal compliance asking for auditability.
4) Can you share SOC 2 attestation and a short note on data retention options?

Also looped in procurement (cc'd) — once we validate perf/quality we may ask for a 30-60 day trial with a small credit.

-Lisa
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Park <lisa@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + benchmark links from today's model-fit call

Great questions — answers below. I pulled the exact benchmark slices and attached the verified profile.

1) trimmed-instruct-7B (quantized) @ seq_len 512 (our test config):
   - batching: dynamic batching with batch_size target 8, concurrency 32 worker threads
   - sustained throughput: ~60 TPS (at seq=512)
   - latency percentiles: p50 110ms, p95 340ms, p99 520ms

2) llama-13b-opt (fp16) tuning notes to keep p95 <200ms:
   - recommended: batch_size 4–6, concurrency 12–16 on an A100/P4d equivalent cluster
   - expected throughput ~18–28 TPS at seq_len 128; at 512 you'll see higher variance — canary with 10k prompt samples first

3) Logs & auditability:
   - By default we provide request/response logs in an auditor-friendly obfuscated form (PII redaction). Raw payloads can be made available under an enterprise contract for security review and on-prem/private deployments.
   - All requests in Hosted/Dedicated are addressable via the Console audit view (searchable, exportable).

4) Compliance docs:
   - SOC 2 Type II attestation is available — I'll send over the latest PDF via your procurement contact (attached in the profile pack).

Attachments included in this message:
- redwood_verified_profile_acme.json (profile + perf slices)
- redwood_benchmarks_acme_20260630.pdf (re-attached)

Quick note on quality regression handling:
- We recommend pinning a small set of key prompts (your "canary" set) in Redwood Console. The system runs nightly evals and triggers alerts if metrics degrade beyond your configured thresholds. For rollouts you can use canary traffic split + automatic rollback on regression to minimize impact.

If helpful I can spin up a hosted trial with a pre-provisioned endpoint and run the attached prompt set from our sandbox so you can see the results immediately. Would Thursday or Friday work for a short follow-up?

Best,
Alex
